title: The Emmaus Road
backstory: After the crucifixion a good man named Joseph took the body of Jesus down and laid it in a tomb cut out of stone, where no one had ever been laid (Luke 23:50-53). The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee saw where his body was put, then went home, prepared spices, and rested the sabbath day (Luke 23:55-56). But Jesus had said beforehand that the Son of man would be put to death, and the third day rise again (Luke 18:33). Now it is very early on the first day of the week, and the women are walking back to the tomb with their spices.

passages.synopsis: Very early on the first day of the week the women came to the tomb with their spices. The stone had been rolled away, and the body of the Lord Jesus was not there. Two men in shining clothes stood by them and asked why they sought the living among the dead, saying he was risen, just as he had told them in Galilee. The women remembered his words and ran to tell the eleven, who thought it sounded like an idle tale, though Peter ran to see the empty tomb for himself.

That same day two of the followers walked to a village called Emmaus, talking over everything that had happened. Jesus himself came alongside them, but they did not recognize him. They told this stranger how their teacher had been condemned and crucified, how they had hoped he would redeem Israel, and how some women had reported a vision of angels. He told them the prophets had said all along that the Christ must suffer and then enter his glory, and he explained the scriptures to them from Moses onward.

As they reached the village the stranger acted as though he would go further, but they urged him to stay because evening was coming. At the table he took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them. Suddenly their eyes were opened, they knew him, and he was gone from their sight. They said their hearts had burned while he talked with them, and they hurried back to Jerusalem, where the others met them with the news that the Lord is risen indeed. Then they told how he was known to them in the breaking of bread.

Jesus reminded his followers that everything written about him in the law, the prophets, and the psalms had to be fulfilled. He opened their understanding so they could grasp the scriptures, and told them that repentance and forgiveness would be preached in his name to all nations. They were his witnesses, and they were to wait in Jerusalem until they were given power from on high. Then he led them out to Bethany, lifted his hands and blessed them, and was carried up into heaven while they worshipped him with great joy.

triviaQuestions.question: What did the women find when they came to the sepulchre?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Luke 24:2 — "And they found the stone rolled away from the sepulchre."

triviaQuestions.question: What did the two men in shining garments tell the women?
options: He is not here, but is risen
triviaQuestions.explanation: Luke 24:6 — "He is not here, but is risen: remember how he spake unto you when he was yet in Galilee,"

triviaQuestions.question: To what village were the two followers walking?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Luke 24:13 — "And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs."

triviaQuestions.question: When did the two finally recognize Jesus?
options: When he called them by name
When he took bread and brake it
triviaQuestions.explanation: Luke 24:31 — "And their eyes were opened, and they knew him; and he vanished out of their sight."

hangmanWords.hint: The village the two were walking to
One of the two who walked with the stranger
He was known to them in the breaking of it
Where Jesus lifted his hands and blessed them

reflection: The two on the road walked for miles with Jesus before they knew him. Where might he already be walking with you?
